# Proverbs 28 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 28:1 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | [The]-wicked flee and-no-one pursues, but-[the]-righteous [are]-bold like-a-young-lion. |
| LOGOS | The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion. |
| PNEUMA | Guilty people run even when nobody's chasing them, but the righteous are as fearless as a lion. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 28:2 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | By-[the]-transgression-of a-land many [are] its-princes, but-by-a-man-of understanding [and]-knowledge, so [the]-established-order endures. |
| LOGOS | When a land transgresses, it has many rulers, but with a man of understanding and knowledge, its stability will long continue. |
| PNEUMA | When a nation sins, it cycles through one leader after another — but a wise, knowledgeable leader brings stability. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 28:4 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Those-forsaking [the]-law praise [the]-wicked, but-those-keeping [the]-law contend with-them. |
| LOGOS | Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law strive against them. |
| PNEUMA | People who abandon God's instruction end up applauding the wicked, but those who follow it stand up and fight them. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 28:7 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | One-keeping [the]-law [is] a-son [who]-understands, but-a-companion-of gluttons shames his-father. |
| LOGOS | The one who keeps the law is a son with understanding, but a companion of gluttons shames his father. |
| PNEUMA | A child who obeys their parents' teaching shows real understanding, but one who hangs out with the wrong crowd humiliates their father. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 28:8 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | One-increasing his-wealth by-interest and-usury — for-one-showing-grace to-[the]-poor he-gathers-it. |
| LOGOS | Whoever multiplies his wealth by interest and profit gathers it for him who is generous to the poor. |
| PNEUMA | If you build wealth through excessive interest, someone who's generous to the poor will end up with it instead. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 28:13 (overlap: 0%)

| PNEUMA | Hide your sins and you'll never succeed. Confess them and leave them behind, and you'll receive mercy. |
